title: Tenant, management groups, subscriptions and resource groups

videos.script: People say they have an Azure account. That sentence hides four boxes, one inside the other. {{boxes}} The outermost box is the tenant. It holds identities: every user, every group, every application. {{tenant}} Inside it hang management groups, like folders. They exist so that a rule set once reaches a whole branch. {{groups}} Then subscriptions. A subscription is the box of money. It gets the bill, and it counts the limits. {{subscription}} And inside a subscription, resource groups. A group holds what lives and dies together. Delete the group, and its contents go with it. {{group}} Every resource has a full name that walks down those boxes. You will take a few apart in your lab. {{id}} Then you will write the shop's tree in Bicep, and the compiler will tell you which box each request is aimed at. {{bicep}} Aim one at the wrong box, and it refuses. That refusal is the one part of the hierarchy your lab can check for real. {{end}}
